title: A Unified Framework for Class-Aware and Class-Agnostic CNN Attribution via Spectral Mapping and Confidence-Adaptive Fusion
content: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has historically diverged into class-aware methods, which highlight discriminative regions for specific target classes, and class-agnostic methods, which capture dominant feature representations regardless of the classification outcome. In this paper, we introduce a unified attribution framework that bridges this gap by explicitly separating the attribution target from the feature extraction operator. Specifically, we project deep activations onto multiple dominant principal components to extract robust, class-agnostic structural maps, while utilizing class-aware gradients to localize target-specific semantics. To synthesize these complementary perspectives, we propose a logit-margin-based fusion mechanism that shifts attribution priority based on the model’s predictive margin. We evaluate our framework in a cross-domain zero-shot setting by applying ImageNet-pretrained architectures (ResNet-50, DenseNet-121) to the Oxford-IIIT Pet dataset. Our zero-shot evaluation shows that the proposed fusion provides an alternative combination of class-aware and class-agnostic evidence. The results suggest that adaptively combining feature-level representation maps with target-driven discriminative maps offers a distinct tool for interpreting CNN representations across domain shifts.
